title: Who's Who: Miriam Vale
summary: Surveyor and instrument maker whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Miriam Vale (1668–1736) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a surveyor and instrument maker whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.
Vale brought a geological surveyor’s habits to the study of odd shadows. Her 1711 manuscript compared the hidden cause of an optical remainder to a buried stratum known only through its effects.
She never claimed to have seen another world, but her careful diagrams outlived the ridicule that greeted them.

For Alderwick readers, Miriam Vale is remembered not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
